claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi possesses severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion increases solute–dislocation interaction strength and solute drag in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The increased solute drag impedes and delays dislocation motion during dynamic loading.
Delayed dislocation motion produces a higher dynamic strain-hardening rate.
Despite the increased drag, sufficient dislocation mobility remains to prevent premature deformation localization.
Preventing premature localization prolongs ductility and produces a strength–ductility balance.
A minor compositional adjustment can reduce lattice distortion without changing phase stability or the overall microstructure.
Reducing lattice distortion diminishes solute drag.
The reduced-distortion alloy will have lower dynamic strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The reduced-distortion alloy will localize deformation earlier than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under dynamic loading, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate than the reduced-distortion compositional variant.
Under dynamic loading, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit delayed localization and maintained ductility relative to the reduced-distortion compositional variant.
The proposed mechanism should operate from a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 through 10^2 s^-1.
The proposed mechanism should operate from room temperature through 400 °C.
The hypothesis is restricted to compositions that remain single-phase solid solutions without secondary phases.
The reduced-distortion alloy serves as the controlled baseline for isolating the effect attributed to lattice distortion.
Comparable strain-hardening rates and ductility in the two alloys would falsify the claim that distortion-enhanced solute drag significantly controls the dynamic response.
